newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans $150 mln, 220 bln lev T-bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans $150 mln, 220 bln lev T-bond issues.

text.p: Bulgaria could issue government bonds worth up to $150 million and 220 billion this year to cover state guarantee on deposits in banks declared insolvent by the courts, figures from the 1997 budget draft showed.

Parliament is expected to approve the bill in principle on Friday and complete it item by item by end-month, prior to the July 1 introduction of an IMF-prescribed currency board system designed to stabilise the economy.
The bonds will be used to cover repayment of deposits in the private TSBank, which was declared bankrupt in March, and another nine banks with ongoing insolvency cases if courts rule them bankrupt.
Under the budget draft the state will use part of proceeds from privatisation to meet interest and principal payments on the bonds. The maturity of the issues was not specified.

Last year the Finance Ministry placed 19.482 billion levs of seven-year T-bonds and $79.105 million of three-year T-bonds with the State Savings Bank and the Bulgarian Post Bank to repay deposits in five banks whose insolvency has been sought by the central bank in May 1996.
Of those five three have been ruled insolvent so far. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88 ($=1,700 Bulgarian levs)
